name: Commercial Air Mover
definition: A portable commercial blower used to accelerate evaporation by directing high-velocity airflow across approved wet carpets, upholstery, floors or building surfaces after cleaning, spills or water-loss work.
includedScope: Portable centrifugal and compact commercial air movers
Carpet-extraction drying and approved water-loss airflow applications
excludedScope: Dehumidifiers, air scrubbers, heaters and HVAC blowers
Ordinary comfort fans without commercial task evidence
Any claim that airflow alone completes structural drying, mould remediation or hygienic decontamination
headline: Commercial air mover airflow, placement, electrical loading and buyer checks
description: This profile explains air-mover formats, airflow reporting, outlet direction, speed, positioning, electrical loading, daisy chaining and the boundary between evaporation and moisture removal.
metaDescription: Commercial air mover guide covering carpet dryers, airflow, speed settings, placement, electrical load, representative models and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not restoration, electrical, mould, indoor-air-quality or structural-drying advice. Air movers can spread contaminants, overload circuits or create trip hazards. Confirm the current manual, electrical listing, site contamination status, placement plan, monitoring method and local requirements before use.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Moves air to accelerate evaporation; it does not remove moisture from the space
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturers position reviewed machines to speed drying after extraction cleaning, spills or water damage.
keyFacts.scope: Named air movers; dehumidifiers are excluded.

keyFacts.label: Airflow reporting
keyFacts.value: CFM, m³/min, m³/h and outlet velocity are not interchangeable claims
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources publish different airflow quantities and units.

keyFacts.label: Electrical planning
keyFacts.value: Current draw, voltage, outlets and daisy-chain limits are model-specific
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources publish distinct amperage and outlet features.

keyFacts.label: Buyer verification
keyFacts.value: Validate placement, electrical load, contamination, noise and measured moisture progress
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer sources describe adjustable positions, speeds and drying uses but not one universal site result.

systemFlow.name: Air intake
systemFlow.role: Admits room air while separating users and debris from moving components.
systemFlow.evidence: Official product and manual sources identify protected housings and fan systems.

systemFlow.name: Motor drive
systemFlow.role: Drives the fan at one or more selected speeds.
systemFlow.evidence: Official specifications publish motor, speed or thermal-protection data.

systemFlow.name: Air acceleration
systemFlow.role: Creates the airflow delivered through the outlet.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish fan or airflow characteristics.

systemFlow.name: Air direction
systemFlow.role: Directs moving air across the intended surface or cavity only where approved.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources identify three or four operating positions.

systemFlow.name: Moisture control
systemFlow.role: Tracks moisture movement and provides removal capacity where required.
systemFlow.evidence: Air-mover sources describe evaporation support, not complete moisture removal.
systemFlow.scope: WCB boundary derived from the disclosed machine function; site plan remains professional responsibility.

variants.name: Traditional centrifugal air mover
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator places and repositions a wheeled or handled blower
variants.spaceConstraints: Intake clearance, outlet path, cord and circuit management
variants.limitations: Large headline airflow may use an unmatched test method.
variants.evidence: Official sources show portable multi-speed blower formats.

variants.name: Compact low-profile blower
variants.taskScale: Tight rooms, spot drying and transport-intensive routes
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator carries, stacks and aims the compact unit
variants.spaceConstraints: Smaller footprint but the same circuit and trip controls apply
variants.limitations: Compact size does not prove lower noise or faster drying.
variants.evidence: Truvox and Minuteman publish compact air-mover formats.

variants.name: Low-wear EC-motor format
variants.taskScale: Occupied or noise-sensitive commercial areas where approved
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator selects speed and monitors access
variants.spaceConstraints: Placement must preserve exits and intake clearance
variants.evidence: Kärcher describes a compact EC-motor blower for faster carpet drying and low-noise use.

performanceMetrics.name: Airflow volume
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal quantity of air moved at a stated speed
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: CFM, m³/min and m³/h can use different test methods and points
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not compare converted units unless measurement conditions match.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish different airflow units.

performanceMetrics.name: Outlet velocity
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Local air speed reported at an unspecified or stated point
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Not the same quantity as volumetric airflow
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: m/s cannot be ranked directly against CFM.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Truvox reports airflow rate in m/s for the reviewed models.

performanceMetrics.name: Speed settings
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Three settings do not imply matched outputs across machines
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Speed count alone does not establish useful drying range.

performanceMetrics.name: Current draw and voltage
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Regional voltage and outlet features differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Daisy chaining is limited by the exact manual, circuit and downstream load.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications publish amperage, voltage or outlet limits.

performanceMetrics.name: Sound and placement
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Occupied-area acceptance and safe route planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Sound values and test methods may be absent or unmatched
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Quiet positioning claims do not replace site measurement.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources describe low-noise or multiple-position use.

applicationFit.assessment: Contamination class, material condition and moisture map should be established before airflow starts.

applicationFit.assessment: Airflow must not create slip, aerosol, dust or pedestrian hazards.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Measured moisture progress at the planned placement and room conditions
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Selecting by the largest airflow number
procurementDecisions.assessment: Compare complete drying trials with matched initial conditions.
procurementDecisions.basis: Airflow units and test points differ, and room conditions affect evaporation.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No normalized drying-time test was found.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Log moisture, RH, temperature, position, speed and elapsed time.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify outlet direction, intake clearance and textile approval.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish differing airflow and positioning data.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Total current, receptacle limits, cord route and circuit protection
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming onboard outlets permit any number of connected machines
procurementDecisions.assessment: Build a circuit schedule from the exact manual and nameplate.
procurementDecisions.basis: Electrical configurations and daisy-chain limits differ.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No universal chain count is established.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Have the planned circuit and downstream load checked before use.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm voltage, amperage, cord, GFCI or local protection and outlet rating.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish different electrical and outlet features.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Contamination assessment, moisture map, dehumidification and completion criteria
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating air movement as moisture removal
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use air movers only as one controlled part of the documented drying system.
procurementDecisions.basis: The machine function accelerates evaporation into the surrounding air.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No remediation result or structural safety is established.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain the responsible professional drying plan and signed completion criteria.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify material condition, airflow path, containment and moisture-removal capacity.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources cite water-damage use but do not establish universal project completion.

engineeringChecks.reason: Multiple air movers can overload a branch circuit or extension arrangement.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Calculate nameplate current and every downstream load against the exact circuit.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources publish model-specific current and outlet features.

engineeringChecks.reason: Airflow can redistribute dust, microbes or other contaminants.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Complete the site's contamination assessment before starting airflow.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers cite water-loss and drying uses; contamination suitability is not established.
engineeringChecks.scope: Actual site and responsible professional decision.

engineeringChecks.reason: Blocked intakes, unstable angles, cords and outlets can create operating hazards.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Follow exact approved positions and maintain intake, exit and pedestrian clearance.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources publish model-specific positions and portability features.

engineeringChecks.reason: A dry-looking surface does not prove concealed materials or the room have reached the target.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Define and record material and ambient readings before, during and after operation.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Air-mover product sources do not provide one universal completion criterion.
engineeringChecks.scope: Actual material system and project plan.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-80:2024
standards.applicability: Electrical-fan safety for products within its household-and-similar scope, including certain appliances used in shops and light industry.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the standard scope and exclusions.
standards.scope: Do not assume it applies to an exact commercial air mover without its conformity documentation.
